content.title: Canadian Lumber Hit With Higher Antidumping Duty
content.summary: The U.S. raised its antidumping duty Tuesday on Canadian lumber imports from most producers to nearly 21% from 7.7%, the sharpest year-over-year increase yet in the long-running softwood trade dispute.  Lumber prices have risen roughly 25% since early May to trade around three-year highs, despite tepid wood demand.  The climb has been fueled by anticipation of the greater antidumping duty as well as a countervailing duty on Canadian lumber that is expected to increase next month.
